title: Public URL setting, secure cookies by default, redirect and link fixes
description: Passkeys bind to an origin, and several things already guess the origin wrongly. Add a public URL setting (PUBLIC_URL env and/or the stored setting from WI-119), required when APP_ENV=production. Use it for: absolute links (getBaseURL in internal/admin/players.go:1037-1043 builds http:// behind Caddy because r.TLS is nil), the VAPID subscriber (hardcoded https://jim.tennis in internal/webpush/webpush.go:273), the iCal UID domain (internal/services/ical_generator.go:38) and later the passkey relying-party ID. Make Secure cookies the default with an explicit development opt-out, instead of depending on APP_ENV=production being set (no tracked compose file sets it). Fix the login redirect: the form posts to /login and drops ?redirect=, and the handler accepts any URL (handlers.go:129) - carry the parameter through and allow only same-site relative paths.

recommended_model.name: Sonnet 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Small targeted fixes with clear test cases.

acceptance_criteria: Production mode refuses to start without a valid https public URL, with a message saying how to set it
Generated player links, calendar files and push configuration use the public URL; no jim.tennis literal remains in Go code
Session cookies are Secure unless development mode is explicitly enabled
After signing in from a protected page the user returns to that page; an absolute or cross-site redirect value is ignored
Existing calendar subscriptions keep working (UID change considered and documented)

notes: Changing iCal UIDs makes calendar apps treat events as new; keep the existing UID domain for jim.tennis by deriving it from the public URL host (which is jim.tennis there).

testing_requirements: Unit tests for redirect validation (relative ok, //host, https://host, backslash variants rejected)

context.user_story: As a club operator, I want the app to know its own address so that links, cookies and passkeys are correct.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
